subject: Latency surge: TLS/connection retries impacting first-token for Nimbus Logistics
messages:
From: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@nimbuslogistics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spikes this morning — first-token takes 1.2-1.8s, timeouts

Aditya —

We started seeing a serious increase in request latencies to your hosted API this morning (~07:45 PDT). P95 for first-token has jumped to ~1.2s and P99 is spiking above 1.7s, and a small number of requests are timing out in our checkout flow. This is affecting our peak batch and impacting conversion.

We've exported a short sample of failing request IDs and tcp traces and attached them: nimbus_latency_samples.csv (10 request rows). The errors look like connection handshake retries — you can see repeated TLS_CLIENT_HELLO attempts in the traces. This looks like an upstream connection issue between your CDN/pop and Redwood's edge or origin.

Can you prioritize? We have a marketing release scheduled this afternoon and need either a mitigation or an ETA.

— Emma
VP Engineering, Nimbus Logistics

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@nimbuslogistics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spikes this morning — first-token takes 1.2-1.8s, timeouts

Emma — thanks for the samples and the heads-up. I'm escalating to SRE and infra immediately and looping in our engineering lead.

Action plan (immediate):
- Rachel/Vivek: can you triage traces and confirm whether the handshake retries are between CDN edge and Redwood upstream?
- If it's a CDN POP regression, can we test routing this customer's traffic to an alternate POP or force longer TLS session resumption TTL?
- I will hold off on public comms until we have a mitigation.

Emma — please confirm if we are OK to reroute a small % of traffic to a different region/pop for a short window (we'll monitor closely).

Attaching the sample you provided to the thread.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@nimbuslogistics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Sudden spikes this morning — first-token takes 1.2-1.8s, timeouts

Aditya / Emma — initial triage below (summary first, details after).

Summary: We see a sharp increase in TLS handshake duration and TCP retransmits for connections originating from the CDN POP serving Nimbus (us-east-1 pop cluster). The pattern looks like periodic TLS renegotiation failures between CDN edge and our gateway pool (connection attempts show 2-3 client_hello retries then success or timeout). P95 TTFT for Nimbus traffic increased from ~140ms to ~780ms in the window 07:40–09:00 PDT; P99 hit ~1.7s. This correlates with a burst of new TLS sessions (low reuse) — session resumption hit rate dropped to ~12% in that window.

Likely causes (shortlist):
- CDN POP started aggressively evicting TLS sessions due to a local cert rotation/cache policy change (we're seeing cert subject/serial flips in the tcp dump).
- Upstream connection pool exhaustion on a subset of our gateway nodes resulting in new TCP/TLS handshakes.
- Intermittent packet loss between CDN edge and our nodes increasing handshake retries.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (risk/ETA):
1) Route Nimbus traffic away from the affected POP to the nearest healthy POP (us-east-2) — low risk / minutes to roll. Will cause minor geo hop but reduces handshake errors while we investigate.
2) Increase connection pool cap and keepalive TTL for the gateway pool serving Nimbus — medium risk / ~15–30m; increases resource usage but reduces new handshake rate.
3) Enable aggressive TLS session resumption (server-side session ticket TTL bump) for customer traffic — medium risk / requires coord with CDN partner for session ticket acceptance / ~30–45m.

Short-term suggestion: we recommend applying (1) immediately and (2) if we still see elevated P95 after routing, then (3). We'll monitor metrics and revert traffic routing when stable.

I attached a tcp dump and a short playbook: tcp-dump-us-east-1-20270402.pcap, mitigation_playbook.md.

Technical details / evidence:
- Sample trace ID req-981234 shows 3 TLS_CLIENT_HELLO attempts with server responses delayed ~250–350ms between attempts.
- Gateway logs show TLS session accept rate dropped from 88% to 12% in the 20m window.
- No changes on our side deployed during the window; change correlation points to upstream (CDN) behavior.

I'll standby to execute routing if you give the go-ahead, Emma.

— Rachel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@nimbuslogistics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spikes this morning — first-token takes 1.2-1.8s, timeouts

Emma — Rachel recommends routing away from the affected POP (us-east-1) immediately and bumping our gateway keepalives. If you approve we'll route ~100% of Nimbus traffic to the adjacent POP (us-east-2) and monitor closely for 30 minutes. If that looks good we'll keep the routing while we work with the CDN partner to restore normal TLS session reuse.

Do you authorize the reroute? If yes, please reply "approve reroute" and we'll kick off now.

Aditya

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 10:19 AM Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@nimbuslogistics.com> wrote:
> Approve reroute — please proceed. Our release is at 13:00 PDT, so anything that stabilizes P95 by then is critical.
> 
> Emma

> VP Engineering, Nimbus Logistics

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation summary: Nimbus — P95/P99 restored, credit / follow-ups

Team / Aditya / Emma (cc):

Executive summary: We routed Nimbus traffic to us-east-2 at ~10:25 PDT and increased gateway keepalive cap. Within two minutes we observed P95 drop from ~780ms to ~160ms and P99 back under ~400ms for Nimbus traffic. Error rate returned to baseline. Attached is a before/after snapshot: ttft_before_after.png.

Customer-impact resolution: mitigated. Thank you to Rachel and the ops team for the quick triage and Rachel for the playbook.

Follow-ups (next 48h):
- SRE to continue tracing with CDN partner and confirm root cause (certificate rotation/POP cache policy vs intermittent packet loss). Rachel to lead.
- Product/CS to discuss goodwill credit for the customer for the hour of elevated latency. Proposed: 10% credit on April invoice. Aditya — please discuss with Emma and confirm.
- Ops: consider increasing session resumption TTL for affected POPs and add an alert if session reuse drops below 40% for >5m.

I'll escalate to our partnerships team to coordinate a postmortem with the CDN vendor if partner-side issues are confirmed.

— Vivek
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ttft_before_after.png

Subject: Re: Post-mitigation summary: Nimbus — P95/P99 restored, credit / follow-ups

Next steps:

- We'll keep your traffic routed to us-east-2 for the next 24h unless you prefer we move back earlier.

Please let me know if the credit is acceptable and whether you want us to move traffic back earlier than 24h.

Regards,
